'''Martin John Taylor''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} (born 18 February 1952)<ref name=whoswho/> is a British mathematician and academic. He was Professor of [[Pure Mathematics]] at the [[School of Mathematics, University of Manchester]] and, prior to its formation and merger, [[University of Manchester Institute of Science and Technology|UMIST]] where he was appointed to a chair after moving from [[Trinity College, Cambridge]] in 1986. He was elected Warden of [[Merton College, Oxford]] on 5 November 2009, took office on 2 October 2010 and retired in September 2018.<ref name="Next warden 2017">{{cite web|url=https://www.merton.ox.ac.uk/news/professor-irene-tracey-named-next-warden|title=Professor Irene Tracey named next warden|publisher=Merton College, Oxford|website=merton.ox.ac.uk|access-date=27 October 2018}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Taylor was born in [[Leicester]] in 1952 and educated at [[Wyggeston Grammar School for Boys|Wyggeston Grammar School]]. He gained a first class degree from the [[University of Oxford]] where he was a student of [[Pembroke College, Oxford]] in 1973, and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] from [[King's College London]] with a thesis on [[Galois representation]]s in 1976 supervised by [[Albrecht Fröhlich]].<ref name=mathgene/><ref name=phd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|first=Martin John|last=Taylor|year=1976|url=https://librarysearch.kcl.ac.uk/permalink/44KCL_INST/3jt0n4/alma990006630680206881|website=kcl.ac.uk|publisher=King's College London|title=Galois module structure of the ring of integers of l-extensions|oclc= 1027487341}}</ref>

== Career and Research ==
Taylor's early research investigated various properties and structures of [[algebraic numbers]]. In 1981 he proved the Fröhlich conjecture relating the symmetries of [[algebraic integer]]s to the behaviour of certain [[analytic function]]s called [[Emil Artin|Artin]] [[L-function]]s. More recently his research has led him to study various aspects of [[arithmetic geometry]]: in particular, he and his collaborators have demonstrated how geometric properties of zeros of integral [[polynomial]]s in many variables can be determined by the behaviour of associated L-functions.

=== Awards and honours===
Taylor was awarded the [[Whitehead Prize]] by the [[London Mathematical Society]] in 1982<ref>{{cite web|title=List of LMS prize winners|url=http://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/list-lms-prize-winners#Whitehead_Prize|publisher=London Mathematical Society|access-date=3 May 2013|date=17 November 2010|website=lms.ac.uk}}</ref>  and shared the [[Adams Prize]] in 1983.<ref name=frs/> He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) in 1996.<ref name=frs>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/martin-taylor-12394/|website=royalsociety.org|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|year=1996|title=Fellows Directory: Sir Martin Taylor FRS|author=Anon}}</ref>  He was President of the London Mathematical Society from 1998 to 2000 and in 2004 was appointed Physical Secretary and Vice-President of the [[Royal Society]].<ref name=frs /> Taylor was appointed [[Knight Bachelor]] in the [[2009 New Year Honours]].<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=58929 |date=31 December 2008 |page=1 |supp=y }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Morgan|first=James|title=Honour for Royal Society luminary|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/sci/tech/7804664.stm|publisher=[[BBC News]]|website=bbc.co.uk|access-date=3 May 2013|date=31 December 2008}}</ref> Taylor received an honorary Doctorate of Science from the University of East Anglia in July 2012.<ref>{{cite web|title=University of East Anglia unveils 2012 honorary graduates|url=http://www.uea.ac.uk/mac/comm/media/press/2012/May/honorary-graduates-2012|publisher=University of East Anglia|access-date=3 May 2013|date=22 May 2012}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Taylor's hobbies include [[fly fishing]] and [[hillwalking|hill walking]],<ref name=whoswho>{{Who's Who | author=Anon | title = Taylor, Sir Martin (John)  | id =U37153 | year = 2025 | doi =10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U37153 | edition = 177th |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford|isbn=9781399411837|oclc=1427336388|pages=2720}}</ref> and he is a supporter of [[Manchester United F.C.]].{{fact|date=March 2026}} He married Sharon Lynn Marlow in 1973 and has four children.<ref name=whoswho/>
